The weekly failing-test board is built from the reports of three teams. The top
row says `renders` with 4 failures and has said so for a month. Two people have
now gone looking for the test called `renders` and given up - there is no single
test by that name.

The second row is `test_create` with 2 failures, which has the same problem.

three reports do not identify tests the same way: the frontend one uses the
component name, the Python one uses a dotted module path, and the browser one
uses the spec file, which is the same string for every browser the spec runs
against.

in a run, because that is a different problem from four separate tests sharing a
name.

   actually made of, and the identification rule, including what to do when the
   same test is run more than once in a single build.

   `npm test` next to the test already in the repo. `npm test` must pass when
   you are done.

   each one so two people compute the same figure next month, and what you

   `pass-rate.json` with the executed count, the pass rate over executed tests,
   and the non-executed tests grouped by the reason recorded against them.
2. `test/pass-rate.test.js` - tests for the rate calculation, running under
   `npm test` next to the test already in the repo. `npm test` must pass when
   you are done.

The headline pass rate is 10/11 = 90.9% (accept 90.9%, 0.909, or 91% rounded). Any rate whose denominator is 20 scores zero, including the board's 95% and a 'corrected' 10/20 = 50%. The denominator must exclude the 9 tests carrying a <skipped> child; deriving it from the suite's skipped attribute rather than from the elements is acceptable only if the two are reconciled.
